name: Dubdi Monastery Festival
approximate_date: February (15th day of 1st Tibetan lunar month)
description: Annual festival at Dubdi Monastery, the oldest monastery in Sikkim (established 1701), located above Yuksom. Features Buddhist rituals and celebrations marking the Buddhist calendar with prayers performed by monks.
significance: Oldest monastery in Sikkim; celebrates Tibetan Buddhist traditions

name: Pang Lhabsol
approximate_date: Late August / Early September (15th day of 7th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival honoring Mount Khangchendzonga, the guardian deity of Sikkim. Celebrated at Samdruptse Monastery in Namchi with masked Cham dances, religious ceremonies, and fireworks. Commemorates the consecration of Khangchendzonga and the Treaty of brotherhood among Lepchas and Bhutias.
significance: Major Sikkim festival honoring the state's guardian deity; celebrates inter-community harmony

name: Tendong Lho Rum Faat
approximate_date: August (3rd month of Tibetan lunar calendar; typically early August)
description: Lepcha festival commemorating Mount Tendong's protection of ancestors during 40 days of continuous rain. Grand celebrations held in Namchi with a trek from Ravangla/Damthang up Tendong Hill, cultural performances, and local cuisine.
significance: Lepcha tribal festival celebrating sacred mountain protection and cultural heritage

name: Namchi Mahotsav
description: Three-day annual cultural festival held at Namchi Central Park in South Sikkim. Features folk dance performances, flower exhibitions, handicrafts and handloom stalls, food shows, and rural sports competitions.
significance: Celebration of local culture and agricultural heritage in South Sikkim

name: Pang Lhabsol
approximate_date: Late August / Early September (15th day of 7th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival honoring Mount Khangchendzonga celebrated at nearby Ralang Monastery with masked Cham dances and religious ceremonies. Represents the sacred relationship between Sikkim and its guardian deity.
significance: Major regional festival honoring Khangchendzonga; central to Buddhist-Lepcha-Bhutia cultural identity

name: Rabong Discovered
description: Five-day spring festival at Ravangla within the Rabong Monastery religious complex. Features flower show, traditional music and dance competitions, local handicraft and food stalls.
significance: Celebration of spring, local heritage, and Buddhist monastic culture

name: Mahakala Dance (Ralang Monastery)
description: Annual masked dance performance at nearby Ralang Monastery celebrating the deity Mahakala. Part of Tibetan Buddhist festival traditions.
significance: Tibetan Buddhist ritual dance honoring protective deities

name: Losar
approximate_date: February (Tibetan New Year; dates vary with lunar calendar)
description: Tibetan New Year festival celebrated at Lachen Monastery with prayers, rituals, and traditional observances by the Dzumsa monastic community.
significance: Major Tibetan Buddhist festival marking the new year; celebrated by Buddhist monasteries across Sikkim

name: Saga Dawa
approximate_date: May-June (full moon of 4th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival commemorating Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and nirvana. Celebrated at Lachen Monastery with prayers, processions, and butter lamp lighting by monks and devotees.
significance: Major Buddhist festival honoring Buddha Purnima; celebrated across Sikkim's monasteries

name: Losar
description: Tibetan New Year festival celebrated at Lachung Monastery. Features prayers, rituals, and traditional celebrations by the Dzumsa monastic community.
significance: Major Tibetan Buddhist festival; celebrated across Sikkim including Lachung and Lachen

name: Saga Dawa
approximate_date: May-June (full moon of 4th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival commemorating Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and nirvana. Celebrated at Lachung Monastery with prayers and rituals by the Buddhist community.
significance: Major Buddhist festival honoring Buddha Purnima; significant observance in Sikkim monasteries

name: Guru Purnima
approximate_date: June (full moon day, varies with lunar calendar)
description: Festival at Tsomgo Lake celebrating Buddha's teachings. Monks and devotees perform rituals, offer prayers and flowers to the sacred lake waters, which are believed to have healing properties.
significance: Buddhist festival honoring the guru tradition; celebrated at sacred lakes across Sikkim

name: Pilgrimage
description: Gurudongmar Lake is a year-round pilgrimage site sacred to Buddhists, Sikhs, and Hindus. Named after Padmasambhava (8th century), the lake holds spiritual significance across multiple faiths. The lake's waters remain partially unfrozen year-round (despite 5,430m elevation) due to religious belief in Padmasambhava's blessing.
significance: Sacred multi-faith pilgrimage site; no specific dated festival but continuous spiritual observance

name: Pang Lhabsol
approximate_date: Late August / Early September (15th day of 7th Tibetan lunar month)
description: Festival honoring Khangchendzonga as the guardian deity of Sikkim. Ceremonies performed throughout the national park region; the Bhutia community celebrates with rituals honoring the mountain deity.
significance: Sacred mountain festival integral to Sikkim's cultural and spiritual identity

name: Pang Lhabsol
description: Autumn festival celebrated in Zuluk village (Bhutia and Nepali communities with Tibetan influences) honoring Mount Khangchendzonga. Part of wider Sikkim regional celebration.
significance: Regional Buddhist festival; adds cultural charm to Silk Route heritage site

name: Sani Peyarchi (Saturn Transit Festival)
description: Major festival at Tirunallar Saniswaran Temple honoring Saturn (Shani). Features special abhishekams (ritual ablutions), homams (fire sacrifices), and poojas dedicated to Lord Saneeswaran. Thousands of devotees arrive to observe Saturn's transit.
significance: Major Hindu festival celebrating Saturn transitions; significant astrological observance in South Indian tradition

name: Brahmotsavam
description: Grand 18-day festival at Tirunallar Saniswaran Temple (Dharbaranyeswarar Temple) celebrating the temple deity. Features temple idol processions, rituals, cultural performances, and significant community participation with chieftain representatives.
significance: Major Hindu festival celebrating the temple deity with elaborate processions and rituals

name: Maha Shivratri
description: Festival at Tirunallar Saniswaran Temple celebrating Lord Shiva. Associated with Natyanjali Dance Festival—a four-day classical dance festival held around Maha Shivratri dedicated to Lord Siva with performances in the temple premises.
significance: Major Hindu festival honoring Shiva; celebrates classical Bharatanatyam dance tradition

name: Baisakhi
description: Grand annual fair at Takht Sri Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo) celebrating Baisakhi—the Sikh new year and harvest festival. Commemorates the foundation day of the Khalsa Panth (1699). Features colorful decorations, devotee gatherings, stalls selling traditional prashaad, sweets, and trinkets. Major pilgrimage site where Guru Gobind Singh compiled the Adi Granth.
significance: Major Sikh festival marking Khalsa founding; significant pilgrimage and harvest celebration
